requirements.requirement: Provide a working IMAP service on node1 for the archive account using a dedicated demonstration password.
requirements.summary: Dovecot is installed from the Alpine 3.23 repository, enabled under OpenRC, listening on port 143, and authenticating the sole archive credential. The account uses a generated password, restricted credential files, and a non-login shell. Service and authentication also recovered after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to authenticate and retrieve both messages while preserving their Message-ID values, bodies, and mailbox.tsv read/unread state.
requirements.summary: Direct IMAP sessions from node2 authenticate successfully and retrieve exactly two messages. one@branch.test contains “Shipment arrived.” with the Seen flag, while two@branch.test contains “Shipment departed.” without Seen. The same complete behavior is demonstrated after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the staged mailbox under /srv/legacy2/imap-maildir-cutover intact.
requirements.summary: The final source tree still contains mailbox.tsv and both messages, and their SHA-256 hashes exactly match the authored baseline. Imported-message hashes also match their respective source messages.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Alpine 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before and after execution and restart. Dovecot 2.4.5-r0 was installed from the matching Alpine 3.23 repositories and operated successfully.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are directly demonstrated. Node2 authenticates to the archive mailbox on node1 and retrieves both messages with correct content, identifiers, and Seen state; the source hashes remain unchanged; and the original OS and kernel remain installed. The provider restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity confirmed by both executor and lifecycle evidence, and recovered service, credentials, mailbox data, and remote retrieval. Operational hygiene is only moderate because of the cleartext all-interface IMAP exposure, an accidental passwd-file corruption that required repair, one failed root-key handoff, a retained troubleshooting package, and leftover reboot logs.
limitations: Final source evidence recaptures file presence and content hashes but not every baseline metadata field such as ownership, permissions, and mtime.
The failed cmd-90451e34fe1d4de3 passwd-edit attempt produced no output, so whether it caused any additional transient mutation cannot be determined.
OpenRC service health is directly demonstrated, but the generic lifecycle failed-services probe is unsupported on Alpine.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The final system is functional, package health shows no new inconsistency, and temporary SSH private-key material was removed. Hygiene is reduced by several executor-caused issues: the failed root SSH handoff added a root authorized key that did not contribute to the solution, though it was later removed (cmd-15446ad5ec194ca5); an attempted archive-shell rewrite malformed /etc/passwd, later repaired and returned to nologin (cmd-bc998796d823472c); dovecot-doc was installed during an unproductive configuration search and remained installed (cmd-179b657671804896); reboot log files were left in /tmp on both nodes (cmd-2d3d422c03674bfa, cmd-eda65e1e9c844132); and the final IMAP configuration exposes cleartext password authentication without TLS on all interfaces, an avoidable security weakness even with a dedicated demonstration password (cmd-b5d2abaf30134694, cmd-a7733d7fd3494072). A second failed passwd-edit command may have rewritten the file, but the trace does not establish whether it caused an additional mutation (cmd-90451e34fe1d4de3).
